verses.text: Jesus answered with another story:
“Heaven’s Kingdom is like a king who prepared a wedding feast for his son.
“He sent his servants to call the invited guests, but they refused to come.
“He sent other servants, saying, ‘Tell the guests, “Dinner is ready. I’ve butchered my cattle and fattened calves. Everything’s ready—come to the wedding feast!”’
“But they brushed it off and went their own way—one to his farm, another to his business.
“The rest grabbed the servants, mistreated them, and killed them.
“The king was furious. He sent his armies, destroyed those murderers, and burned their city.
“Then he told his servants, ‘The wedding feast is ready, but the people I invited weren’t worthy.
“‘Go to the street crossings and invite everyone you find to the feast.’
“The servants went out on the roads and gathered everyone they found, good and bad alike. The wedding hall filled with guests.
“When the king came in to see the guests, he noticed a man who wasn’t wearing wedding clothes.
“He asked, ‘Friend, how did you get in here without wedding clothes?’ The man had nothing to say.
“Then the king told his servants, ‘Tie his hands and feet, take him out, and throw him into the outer darkness.’ That’s where people will weep and grind their teeth.
“Many are invited, but few are chosen.”
Then the Pharisees went and planned how to trap Jesus with his own words.
They sent their disciples to him with the Herodians. They said, “Teacher, we know you’re honest and teach God’s way truthfully, without playing favorites.
“So tell us: is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar or not?”
Jesus knew their bad intentions. “Why are you testing me, you hypocrites?
“Show me the coin used for the tax.” They brought him a denarius.
He asked them, “Whose face and name are on it?”
They said, “Caesar’s.” He told them, “Then give Caesar what belongs to Caesar, and give God what belongs to God.”
When they heard this, they were amazed. They left him and went away.
That same day, Sadducees—who say there’s no resurrection—came and questioned him.
They said, “Teacher, Moses said, ‘If a man dies without children, his brother must marry the widow and raise children for him.’
“There were seven brothers among us. The first married and died without children, leaving his wife to his brother.
“The same happened with the second and third, right through the seventh.
“After them all, the woman died too.
“So in the resurrection, whose wife will she be? All seven married her.”
Jesus answered, “You’re mistaken because you don’t know the Scriptures or God’s power.
“In the resurrection, people don’t marry or get married. They’re like God’s angels in heaven.
“About the resurrection of the dead, haven’t you read what God told you?
“‘I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.’ God isn’t the God of the dead—he’s the God of the living.”
When the crowds heard this, they were amazed at his teaching.
When the Pharisees heard Jesus had silenced the Sadducees, they gathered together.
One of them, an expert in the Law, tested Jesus with a question:
“Teacher, which commandment in the Law is the greatest?”
Jesus answered, “‘Love the Lord your God with all your heart, all your soul, and all your mind.’
“That’s the first and greatest commandment.
“The second is like it: ‘Love your neighbor as yourself.’
“The whole Law and the Prophets hang on these two commandments.”
While the Pharisees were gathered together, Jesus asked them a question:
“What do you think about the Christ? Whose son is he?” They said, “David’s.”
He asked, “Then how does David, speaking by the Spirit, call him Lord?
“‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at my right hand until I put your enemies under your feet.”’
“If David calls him Lord, how can he be David’s son?”
No one could answer him. From that day on, no one dared ask him any more questions.
